column3: Shares the Day of meeting God but presents it as the endpoint of hypocrisy, a negative counterpart to the believers' peace.
Describes the enduring excellent abode that frames the noble reward named in the focus.
Explicitly identifies the believers' greeting in Paradise as peace, closely paralleling the focus.
States that the patient are received in Paradise with greeting and peace, directly matching the focus's welcome.
The immediate context calls believers to abundant remembrance before God's merciful address and greeting.
Shows God's servants answering ignorance with peace, an earthly ethical counterpart to the promised greeting.
The prepared blazing fire contrasts with the focus's prepared noble reward but does not clarify its content.
Uses the exact phrase noble reward for a divinely multiplied return, supporting the reward dimension.
Explicitly says the believers' greeting in the gardens is peace.
Links peace to birth, death, and resurrection for Jesus, but not to the believers' meeting with God.
Completes the immediate command to remember and glorify God that precedes the focus.
Calls a royal letter noble, with no material connection to the promised reward or greeting.
Its preparation of painful punishment for disbelievers only contrasts with the focus's noble reward.
Establishes the obligation to return a greeting with equal or better goodwill, illuminating the social force of peace-greeting.
Uses casting a statement before false partners, unrelated to the meeting and peace of the focus.
Promises obedient women a doubled reward and noble provision, a close local instance of prepared generous recompense.
The immediately preceding verse describes God's mercy in bringing believers from darkness to light, directly leading into their greeting.
Contrasts voluntary worship with humiliation but does not address the peaceful welcome of believers.
Prepared humiliating punishment for those who harm God and His messenger is only an opposite outcome.
God's knowledge of unseen and deeds does not materially develop the focus's meeting, greeting, or reward.
The deniers' refusal to hope for meeting God provides a negative counterpart to the believers' anticipated meeting.
Promises believers who do good a great reward, supporting the focus's reward motif.
The immediate sequel names the Prophet as witness, bearer of good news, and warner, extending the focus's promised good outcome.
Depicts compelled submission on the Day, contrasting with the secure peace of the focus.
Pairs warning with good news to believers who do righteous deeds and receive a good reward.
Promises charitable believers a multiplied return and noble reward, closely echoing the focus's recompense.
Narrates Abraham and Ishmael's submission without addressing the meeting with God or its greeting.
Announces peace on the days of birth, death, and resurrection, a limited parallel to the focus's Day-of-meeting peace.
The immediate continuation presents the Prophet as a caller to God and illuminating lamp, developing the surrounding promise.
Uses being sound or secure for a missed call to prostration, not the believers' final greeting.
Promises avoidance of major sins will lead to entry into a noble entrance, supporting the honorable final reward.
The immediate continuation explicitly commands the Prophet to give believers good news of God's great bounty.
The angels greet the patient with peace at their final abode, closely clarifying the focus's greeting.
Promises the foremost believers gardens prepared for them, a related image of lasting divine reward.
Calls the greeting exchanged on entering homes a blessed and good greeting from God, illuminating its divine character.
Describes God as most generous, but not the prepared noble reward in the focus.
Prepared Hell for hypocrites and idolaters is an opposite outcome rather than positive support.
Defines honor by piety, without developing the final peace-greeting or reward.
Speaks of those certain they will meet their Lord and return to Him, directly supporting the encounter motif.
Requires noble speech to parents, an ethical use of noble language unrelated to the final reward.
Promises believing righteous people gardens of bliss, providing the setting elaborated in the following greeting verse.
Universal submission and return to God provide only a broad background for the focus's peaceful meeting.
Promises firmly believing, worshipping people a great reward, a nearby recompense parallel.
Affirms revealed truth and earlier scripture, with no material link to the focus's promised greeting.
Calls the scripture-bearers noble and righteous, a different use of nobility.
Contrasts one who meets a good promise with one summoned to judgment, clarifying meaningful final encounter.
Describes the sudden end of worldly life and God's command, not the believers' peaceful welcome.
Expresses command to be first among those submitting, without a link to final greeting or reward.
Promises a great reward to those who strive in God's way, supporting the recompense theme.
The earth casting out its contents is resurrection imagery but adds little to the focus.
Promises a good reward for obedience, offering a related conditional divine recompense.
Angels greet the righteous with peace and command their entrance into Paradise, directly paralleling the focus.
A peace greeting to Moses and Aaron is honorific, not the believers' final greeting.
Its ambiguous reference to meeting Moses or the Book does not clarify the focus's encounter with God.
A peace greeting to Abraham marks prophetic honor but is not the eschatological welcome of the focus.
Hypocrites meet believers with a false public confession, a distant contrast to genuine peace.
Mentions the Day of Resurrection within Satan's threat, without relation to the focus's reward.
Condemns failure to honor the orphan, a different use of honor from the noble reward.
A peace greeting to Noah is an honorific parallel but does not develop the focus's final scene.
Praises calling to God and identifying as Muslim, only broadly related to the local prophetic sequence.
Moses casting down his staff does not materially connect to the focus.
Describes deceptive encounters and concealed revelation, a negative social contrast to genuine greeting.
God fully pays believers their rewards and increases them from His bounty, supporting the reward dimension.
Promises believers forgiveness and noble provision, closely paralleling the focus's noble recompense.
Describes an enduring burden on the Day of Resurrection, an opposite outcome with limited relevance.
Says death will meet people and return them to the Knower of the unseen, clarifying unavoidable encounter.
Promises believers mercy, pleasure, and abiding gardens, a related expression of their final reward.
The detailed description of the cow does not materially connect to the focus.
Promises believers forgiveness and noble provision, closely echoing the focus's prepared noble reward.
Commands believers to enter wholly into peace, an ethical counterpart to the focus's final peace.
Describes the idolaters' surrender on that Day, a negative and compelled contrast.
A peace greeting to Elias is an honorific parallel but not the believers' final greeting.
The call to give thanks for produce does not clarify the focus.
Frames submission to God and the messenger's duty of delivery, supporting the surrounding prophetic call in Al-Ahzab.
Promises true believers forgiveness and noble provision, a close parallel to the focus's recompense.
Denies coolness and nobility to the condemned, a limited opposite to the noble reward.
The question about demanding payment does not materially connect to the focus.
Tells deniers to continue until they meet their promised Day, a negative counterpart to the focus's meeting.
Names the believers' final dwelling the abode of peace with their Lord, strongly supporting the focus's peace.
Reports a fearful plea while looking toward the Fire, an opposite eschatological scene.
Describes bodily testimony on the Day, with no material connection to greeting or reward.
Records believers affirming the revealed truth and their prior submission, a broad basis for the promised outcome.
Prepared immense punishment for deliberate murder is only the opposite of the noble reward.
A word of peace from a merciful Lord directly illuminates the divine peace-greeting of the focus.
Promises the submitted doer of good a reward with his Lord and freedom from fear and grief.
Makes coming to God with a sound heart the decisive condition, directly related to the final encounter.
In the same surah, God prepares a great reward for women who choose God, His messenger, and the Hereafter.
Rejecting God's signs and meeting Him leads to loss of mercy and painful punishment, a clear negative counterpart.
Denial of meeting the Lord nullifies deeds, negatively reinforcing the importance of that meeting.
God guides followers of His pleasure to paths of peace and brings them from darkness to light, echoing the immediate context.
Promises that no believer's work is lost and rewards them with gardens, supporting the final recompense.
Explicitly affirms that the appointed time of meeting God is coming, directly clarifying the focus's encounter.
Promises that every sacrifice is recorded so God may reward believers with their best deeds.
Contrasts Muslims with criminals in judgment but adds little to the focus's peace and reward.
Begins the scene of people fleeing on the Day, a distant eschatological contrast.
Addresses human deception concerning the noble Lord, not the focus's noble reward.
Mentions the day two armies met by God's permission, a different kind of meeting.
Names God as Peace and source of security, providing theological background for the promised greeting.
Sleep and seeking provision day and night do not materially connect to the focus.
Uses peace as the direct assurance given to the companions of the right, closely paralleling the focus's welcome.
Promises believers gardens and lasting purity, supplying the broad setting of the focus's noble reward.
Identifies believers who do good as enduring companions of the Garden, a related final outcome.
Directly tells believers to know that they will meet God, supporting the encounter motif.
Describes those certain they will meet God, linking that certainty to faithful perseverance.
Promises God-fearing people gardens, purity, and God's pleasure, a closely related final reward.
Denies God will speak to, look at, or purify covenant-breakers on the Day, a strong negative contrast to the believers' peaceful meeting.
Calls believers toward forgiveness and a Paradise prepared for the God-fearing.
Places full recompense on the Day of Resurrection and identifies entry into Paradise as true success.
Promises believing righteous people enduring gardens, a related expression of the focus's reward.
Promises obedience to God and the messenger leads to the company of those favored by God.
Rewards truthful confession with gardens beneath which rivers flow, a related final recompense.
Portrays denial of meeting God as final loss, a direct negative counterpart to the focus's encounter.
Describes the people of Paradise praising God after being guided into the final inheritance.
Records the people of the heights greeting the people of Paradise with peace.
Announces to the humble that they will enter Paradise without fear or grief.
Treats forgetting the meeting of this Day as grounds for divine abandonment, a negative counterpart.
States that denying God's signs and meeting Him nullifies deeds, directly underscoring the encounter.
Promises believers gardens, good dwellings, and God's approval, a closely related final blessing.
Contrasts those who do not hope for meeting God and are content with worldly life.
Promises those who do good the best reward and more, with no gloom or humiliation on their faces.
Promises those who believe, do good, and humble themselves before their Lord an eternal Garden.
Shows the righteous entering gardens of perpetual residence as angels come to them from every gate before the peace greeting of 13:24.
Describes the Paradise promised to the God-fearing as an enduring garden.
Places the God-fearing in gardens and springs, establishing the setting of secure final reception.
Commands the God-fearing to enter Paradise in peace and security, directly paralleling the focus.
Promises believing righteous people the gardens of Paradise as their lodging.
Directly connects hope for meeting the Lord with righteous action and undivided worship.
Promises repentant believers gardens of Paradise, a related final reward.
Describes the Garden of Eden promised by the Most Merciful to His servants.
Says the people of Paradise hear no vain speech there, only peace, directly illuminating the focus's greeting.
Promises the believer who comes to God with righteous deeds the highest ranks.
Names the gardens of Eden and their abiding life as the reward of those purified.
Describes the righteous kept far from Hell, secure even from the greatest terror.
Promises believers entry into gardens, where they are honored with adornment and fine clothing.
Declares the believers successful, introducing their inheritance of the highest garden.
Names the believers inheritors of al-Firdaws, where they remain forever.
Calls the eternal Garden promised to the God-fearing their reward and destination.
Promises believing righteous people lofty rooms in Paradise with rivers beneath them.
States that many people disbelieve in meeting their Lord, a direct negative counterpart.
Promises believing righteous people gardens of refuge as recompense for their deeds.
Treats forgetting the meeting of this Day as the reason for punishment, directly contrasting the focus.
Describes believers entering gardens of perpetual residence in an honorable final reception.
Reports the keepers of Paradise greeting its arrivals with peace and commanding their eternal entry.
Prays for believers and their righteous relatives to enter the gardens of Eden promised to them.
Has angels assure steadfast believers not to fear or grieve and give them glad news of the promised Paradise.
Presents the angels as believers' guardians in this world and the Hereafter, confirming their promised Paradise.
Calls Paradise a hospitable gift from the Forgiving, Merciful, complementing the focus's noble reward.
Names doubt about meeting the Lord, directly contrasting the certainty implied by the focus.
Addresses God's servants on the final Day with freedom from fear and grief.
Commands believers and their spouses to enter Paradise in joy, closely matching the focus's final welcome.
Links punishment to forgetting the meeting of this Day, a direct negative counterpart.
Promises that God will admit the believers into the Paradise He has made known to them.
Brings Paradise near for the God-fearing, immediately preparing the command of peaceful entry.
Commands the God-fearing to enter Paradise in peace and identifies it as the Day of Eternity.
Places the God-fearing in gardens and bliss, a related final condition.
Places the God-fearing amid gardens and rivers.
Locates them in a seat of truth near an all-powerful Sovereign, closely related to meeting God in honor.
Promises two gardens to the one who fears standing before the Lord.
Promises the foremost comfort, fragrance, and a garden of bliss, providing the adjacent positive outcome before 56:91.
Names the garden of bliss as the foremost person's final destination.
On the Day believers' light runs before them and they receive glad news of enduring gardens.
Calls believers to a forgiveness and Paradise as vast as heaven and earth.
On the Day of Gathering, promises believers entry into enduring gardens and calls it the great success.
Describes the successful person's lofty garden, a related final reward.
Says God protects the righteous from the evil of that Day and grants them radiance and joy.
Rewards their patience with a garden and silk.
Identifies the Garden as their reward and declares their striving appreciated.
Promises the God-fearing success, followed by gardens and other delights.
Places the righteous in bliss, a related final state of reward.
Describes faces on that Day as joyful and satisfied with their effort.
Calls the reassured soul to return to its Lord, pleased and pleasing, directly clarifying a peaceful encounter with God.
Commands that soul to enter God's Paradise, completing the final welcome begun in 89:27.
Promises the believers gardens of perpetual residence as their reward with their Lord.
